title: Reversible computing
summary: The physical floor on energy per bit, and logic that can recycle its own energy.

links.why: logic that recycles its own energy

ideas.how: erasing a bit has a minimum energy cost, set by physics

then: Landauer (1961) shows that erasing a bit must cost energy.
Reversible logic is understood in theory (Bennett, 1973), but chips stay irreversible.
A 22 nm reversible test chip (2025) recovers part of its switching energy.
Projection: reversible chips must show savings at gigahertz speeds to leave the lab.

challenges.title: Approach the Landauer limit
challenges.task: How slowly must a gate switch to save 100× energy?

ask: What is the Landauer limit in simple terms?
Why are ordinary logic gates irreversible?
